sourceBindings.text: Treat three reports as three cases
A is sandy loam/pH 5.8/low N/low OM; B is clay loam/pH 7.2/high N/high OM; C is silty/pH 6.5/waterlogging-prone.
A: carrots and potatoes are plausible with moisture and nutrient management; a high-demand corn crop may be lower fit if low N stays uncorrected, not inherently impossible.
B: broccoli and corn are possible if structure/drainage and other nutrients suit; a deep straight-rooted crop may be lower fit under confirmed compaction.

C: rice and willow are the two source examples, each only conditional on a suitable local species/cultivar, climate and water system. Willow is a non-food tree, not a second verified food crop. If the task is restricted to food crops, this model is incomplete until a second locally justified food candidate is supplied; do not invent one. A waterlogging-sensitive candidate can be lower fit with reasons. Carrots would be lower fit if root-zone waterlogging persists; verify drainage, rooting conditions and the local season before accepting or changing that comparison.
Report values stay separate from physical sample identities; every row needs reasons and a missing test.
